summary: This document describes a workflow for adding internal links to blog articles. The process involves selecting articles to work on, running a checking tool that suggests link targets, manually choosing the most relevant links based on the article's content (not just word matches), inserting those links inline in the prose, verifying they point to real articles, and finally reporting what was done.

explanations.16: The grep command searches through blog and draft folders for any index file whose frontmatter contains a `slug:` field matching the user's input, helping convert a slug name into an actual file path.
explanations.26: This git command finds article files that have been recently modified or newly created in the working directory, then extracts just the file paths so we know which articles need link updates.
explanations.30: This is a fallback: if nothing is currently edited, look at the last commit to see which articles were changed then, treating that as the work scope.
explanations.39: The `!!` markers are visual warnings that flag links which point to non-existent article slugs — these are mistakes that need fixing before proceeding.
explanations.42: AnythingLLM is an AI tool being used here to analyze semantic similarity, not just word overlap, to suggest better link targets than a purely lexical approach would find.
explanations.45: A candidate with `meaning: not close` matched because it contains the same words as the current article, but the AI judged the actual topic or meaning as unrelated, so it's likely noise.
explanations.62: This is a local file that maps out the blog's structure (main topics and series) so you can spot related articles the script may have underscored because they use different terminology.
explanations.73: The `<Link>` component is a special React/Docusaurus tag that creates the actual hyperlink; you don't need to manually import it because it's registered globally in the project.
explanations.87: Running the Docusaurus build catches broken internal links early because the build process validates all link targets exist, faster than finding them later when readers hit dead links.
